newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs back environmental protection plan.
newsitem.headline: MEPs back environmental protection plan.

text.p: The European Parliament gave a second reading on Tuesday to a plan to finance environmental protection in developing countries, but demanded a string of improvements to the scheme.

The plan -- COM(95)294 -- is designed to prevent disasters such as the dangerous dispersal of toxic waste, the use of hazardous chemicals, the contamination of vital water resources and the destruction of forests and fertile soils.
MEPs complained that the planned budget for the scheme -- 15 million Ecus over three years -- was a paltry sum which was unlikely to alter non-sustainable practices in developing countries.
They called for an increase in the funding to 50 million Ecus by the year 2000.
Commissioner Christos Papoutsis said the Commission could take on board most of parliament's amendments.
He agreed the scheme should give priority to health protection and reducing the environmental damage of human activity.
